_comment: Example Claude-Code settings.json hooks fragment. JSON has no comments, so notes live in _comment keys (Claude Code ignores unknown keys). Merge the hooks block into your own settings.json.
_comment_behavior_layer: The behavior layer is NOT delivered by a hook, and this is deliberate. Load it from your instructions file instead: copy `behavior-layer.example.md` into your project as `behavior-layer.md` and add a single line `@behavior-layer.md` to your CLAUDE.md (or paste the layer inline if your tool has no import syntax). WHY NOT A HOOK: a SessionStart hook that prints the file (`cat behavior-layer.md`) looks like it works, but a hook's output is capped — the Claude Code docs give 10,000 characters — and past the cap the assistant is handed a file path and a preview of up to the first 2,000 characters, not the text, and Claude Code does not ask it to open the file. The example layer is under that cap today but not by much, and a layer you extend is the one that crosses it; a half-delivered layer looks installed. An instructions-file import is expanded and loaded into context at launch — it is not hook output, so the hook cap does not apply to it. Do not re-add a SessionStart hook here for this purpose.

hooks._comment_PreToolUse: A PreToolUse command hook can validate a tool argument against an allowlist and BLOCK the call (exit non-zero) before it runs — e.g. guarding a tag / label set so only an approved vocabulary is ever written. Point its command at your own validator script. Shown here as a commented pattern, not active. Hooks are the right tool for GATING a call; they are the wrong tool for injecting a large block of text.
